Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Windstorm Week and Weather Suspicions", "body": "Chance opened by saying the show was an open call in line because the planned guests lost power in a Colorado windstorm. One of the hosts tied the ace of swords to the wind, and Chance said the gusts had been crazy in Missouri too. A caller argued that engineered weather and cell towers were behind the chaos and said he was hearing of more and bigger tower gifting than ever. Several voices described heat, cold and storms across the Southwest and Midwest, and the group debated whether the severity was meant to push a climate narrative."}, {"title": "Sound, Electricity, and the Earth's Immune System", "body": "Chance explained that his sound healing with tuning forks works as a low amperage form of electricity, which helps him find communication breakdowns in the field rather than anything physical. He suggested this might relate to Sheldrake's morphogenetic fields and argued that the Earth has a similar energetic body. Chance said that if people clearing blockages with earth pipes ever triggered upheaval, it would be the planet's own immune system responding, not anyone's fault. He also answered a chat question about aluminum tuning forks and said he had no information beyond intuition either way."}, {"title": "Deep Time, Erosion, and Mythic Volcanoes", "body": "Chance showed a short book by a geologist who, as Chance described it, argued the Earth is far younger than four and a half billion years, citing coastal erosion rates and rapidly fossilized remains. One speaker suggested electrolysis and a growing Earth could explain both lost coastlines and new land. Another participant then proposed that the Greek myth of Typhon and Mount Etna recorded an electrical event behind the Grand Canyon, and that Yellowstone was the volcano at the center of that story."}, {"title": "Astrology, Archetypes, and Rooting Deeper", "body": "Kayleigh sent a voicemail linking the weather to Jupiter and Saturn in Aquarius, Uranus in Taurus, and the final Saturn and Uranus square of the year, which she compared to an explosion meeting a brick wall. One speaker responded that the people pulling the levers might be instruments of archetypal timing rather than masterminds. Later Rachel, back from recording a runes conversation with Ben, named the ice rune as a favorite for its present moment stillness and said the wind makes trees root deeper and prunes what no longer belongs."}, {"title": "Green Man Symbolism and Crypto Doubts", "body": "One of the hosts read a passage from a book tying the green man, Gabriel, the dragon and death symbolism together, and the talk moved on to Pan, Hellier and the Green Knight. Later the conversation turned to Rokfin and cryptocurrency. Voices complained about fees and confusing wallets, Chance said he had converted his tokens to Ethereum and Bitcoin but not to cash, and one participant read a dictionary sense of crypto as a secret adherent to a creed. Several urged listeners to understand the system whether or not they joined it."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight's Vibe Rant is a call-in show with open lines and open minds. The only thing I want to figure out, is why it's so damn windy.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I'm so glad you showed up and also the people who are watching it later. I've been hitting you with a lot lately.
